sentence: Empagliflozin is a prescription medicine used to treat type 2 diabetes, heart failure and chronic kidney disease.
note: NHS page title: treats type 2 diabetes, kidney disease and heart failure; NHS about page: only available on prescription.

sentence: It is a sodium-glucose co-transporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitor, and its brand name is Jardiance.
note: Gateshead Health title lists empagliflozin among SGLT2 inhibitors; NHS: brand name Jardiance.

sentence: The main cautions include thrush, dehydration when it is combined with diuretics, and a serious build-up of ketones called diabetic ketoacidosis, which the NHS says needs a 999 call if suspected.
note: NHS side-effects: thrush common, DKA serious; SmPC: may add to diuretic effect with dehydration risk; NHS main page: call 999 if DKA suspected.

sentence: Type 2 diabetes, to lower blood sugar levels
note: NHS: used for type 2 diabetes; MedlinePlus: lowers blood sugar.

sentence: Heart failure, including symptomatic chronic heart failure as recommended by NICE
note: NICE TA773/TA929: option for symptomatic chronic heart failure.

sentence: Chronic kidney disease in adults, as recommended by NICE under specific conditions
note: NICE TA942: option for CKD in adults only if conditions are met.

sentence: Empagliflozin is a type of medicine known as a sodium-glucose co-transporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitor.
In diabetes it lowers blood sugar by helping remove extra sugar from the body through the urine.
note: NHS: helps remove sugar through pee; MedlinePlus: kidneys get rid of more glucose in the urine.

sentence: In heart failure it reduces the amount of work the heart has to do.
The NHS says it starts to lower blood sugar after about 1 to 2 hours and may take up to a week to work fully, while in heart failure it can be a month or 2 before symptoms improve.
The NHS lists thrush, needing to pee more often, feeling more thirsty than usual and skin rash as common side effects.
The NHS says low blood sugar can happen if meals are skipped, alcohol is drunk or other diabetes medicines are taken.
note: Search summary of NHS side-effects page: low blood sugar can happen with skipped meals, alcohol or other diabetes medicines.

sentence: Diabetic ketoacidosis can make a person feel very thirsty, confused or unusually tired, or give breath that smells sweet, and the NHS says to call 999 if it is suspected; Diabetes UK describes it as a rare side effect.
note: NHS symptoms; NHS main page: 999 for suspected DKA; Diabetes UK: rare, call 999 or A&E for DKA signs.

sentence: Fournier's gangrene is a rare but serious genital infection that can cause severe pain, tenderness, redness or swelling in the genital area with a high temperature or feeling unwell; the NHS says to call 999 if it is suspected, and its side-effects page says to tell a doctor or call 111 straight away.
note: NHS main page 999; NHS side-effects page 111 straight away; Diabetes UK: rare but serious.

sentence: A serious allergic reaction (anaphylaxis), with swelling of the lips, mouth, throat or tongue or difficulty breathing, needs a 999 call.
note: NHS: sudden swelling of lips, mouth, throat or tongue, struggling to breathe: call 999.

sentence: The NHS says to call 111 straight away for signs of dehydration.
note: NHS: dehydration signs, call 111 straight away (search summary).

sentence: The NHS says most adults can take it, and suggests checking with a doctor for people aged 75 or older.
note: NHS who-can page: most adults can take it, check with a doctor if 75 or older.

sentence: It is not used to treat type 1 diabetes.
note: NHS: not used for type 1 diabetes.

sentence: The NHS lists a past allergic reaction, low blood pressure, severe kidney or liver disease, frequent urinary tract infections and upcoming surgery as reasons to check with a doctor first.

NHS information lists diuretics (water tablets) and blood pressure medicines among medicines that interact with it, and the UK product information says it may add to the diuretic effect of thiazide and loop diuretics and may increase the risk of dehydration and low blood pressure.
note: NHS summary lists diuretics and blood pressure medicines as interacting; SmPC: may add to thiazide/loop diuretic effect and increase dehydration/hypotension risk.

sentence: The NHS says it is not recommended in pregnancy because there is little information about whether it could affect the baby, and not usually recommended while breastfeeding because it is not known how much passes into breast milk.
note: NHS pregnancy page: little information; breastfeeding not usually recommended, not known how much passes into milk.

sentence: The NHS says the tablets may need to be stopped before an operation if eating has to stop, and during recovery, because of the risk of diabetic ketoacidosis.
note: NHS common questions: may need to stop before operation/while recovering because of DKA risk.

sentence: The NHS says alcohol can be drunk with it, but alcohol can increase the risk of low blood sugar and of side effects such as diabetic ketoacidosis, so it advises trying to limit how much is drunk.
An NHS hospital trust leaflet says that passing more glucose in the urine increases the risk of a urinary tract infection.
note: East Kent Hospitals leaflet: more glucose in urine increases UTI risk.

sentence: For chronic heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, NICE says a heart failure specialist should advise on starting empagliflozin and monitoring should be done by the most appropriate healthcare professional.
Empagliflozin is used to treat type 2 diabetes, heart failure and chronic kidney disease.
Its brand name is Jardiance, and it is not used for type 1 diabetes.
It comes as tablets, and the NHS says it is only available with a prescription.
note: NHS about page: tablets, prescription only.

sentence: For heart failure, NICE recommends it as an option for symptomatic chronic heart failure, both with reduced ejection fraction and with preserved or mildly reduced ejection fraction.
NICE says treatment should start on the advice of a heart failure specialist.
note: TA929: started on advice of HF specialist; TA773: specialist should advise on starting.

sentence: Where several options are suitable, including dapagliflozin, NICE guidance on preserved or mildly reduced ejection fraction says the least expensive should be used.

For chronic kidney disease, NICE recommends it for adults only under specific conditions, including as an add-on to optimised standard care with the highest tolerated licensed dose of an ACE inhibitor or ARB, unless those are contraindicated.
note: TA942 conditions (eGFR/albumin criteria not stated here).

sentence: The NHS says treatment for diabetes, heart failure or chronic kidney disease is usually for life.
note: NHS about page: usually for life.

sentence: Empagliflozin is a sodium-glucose co-transporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitor.
In diabetes it helps remove extra sugar from the body through the urine, so blood sugar falls.
In heart failure it reduces the work the heart has to do.
The NHS says it starts to work after about 1 to 2 hours to lower blood sugar, but it may take up to a week to work fully.
In heart failure it might be a month or 2 before symptoms improve, and the NHS says it is still reducing the heart's workload even if no change is noticed.
note: NHS: month or 2; still reducing heart workload.

sentence: The NHS says it does not make people put on weight, and some people lose weight.
The NHS advises against stopping it without talking to a doctor first.
note: NHS about page: advises against stopping without talking to a doctor.

sentence: The NHS lists thrush, needing to pee more often, feeling thirstier than usual and skin rash as the common side effects.
The NHS says a pharmacist can recommend an antifungal treatment for thrush.
The NHS says low blood sugar can happen if meals are skipped, alcohol is drunk or other diabetes medicines are taken.
The NHS describes more serious side effects as rare.
note: NHS about page: more serious side effects rare.

sentence: Diabetic ketoacidosis, where ketones build up in the body, can cause great thirst, confusion, unusual tiredness or sweet-smelling breath, and the NHS lists feeling or being sick, stomach pain and deeper or faster breathing among other signs.
The NHS says to call 999 if diabetic ketoacidosis, anaphylaxis or Fournier's gangrene is suspected.

Fournier's gangrene, a serious genital infection, can cause severe pain, tenderness, redness or swelling in the genital area with a high temperature or feeling unwell, and the NHS side-effects page says to tell a doctor or call 111 straight away.
note: NHS side-effects page wording; main page says 999.

sentence: Sudden swelling of the lips, mouth, throat or tongue, or struggling to breathe, may be anaphylaxis and needs a 999 call.
The NHS says to call 111 straight away for signs of dehydration.
NHS information lists diuretics and medicines that lower blood pressure among medicines that interact with empagliflozin.
The UK product information says it may add to the diuretic effect of thiazide and loop diuretics and may increase the risk of dehydration and low blood pressure.
The NHS says people can drink alcohol while taking empagliflozin, but alcohol can increase the risk of low blood sugar levels.
It advises trying to limit how much alcohol is drunk, because alcohol can increase the risk of side effects such as diabetic ketoacidosis.
The NHS says the tablets may need to be stopped before an operation if eating has to stop, and while recovering afterwards, because of the risk of diabetic ketoacidosis.
An NHS hospital trust leaflet says that passing more glucose in the urine increases the risk of a urinary tract infection.
The NHS says most adults can take empagliflozin and suggests checking with a doctor for people aged 75 or older.

The NHS says it is not suitable for people with type 1 diabetes or at higher risk of diabetic ketoacidosis.
